budget_items.what_was_said: A board member confirmed the town used grant money, not its own funds, to pay the consultant who drafted the MBTA Communities bylaw language.

budget_items.topic: 40R smart growth annual payment for Tritown
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident asked whether the town's annual 40R payment (tied to the Tritown smart growth district) would be lost by adding the new MBTA overlay; the chair said it should continue since the underlying development and its 40R filings are unaffected.
In discussing development pressure, a board member cited the current median home assessment as an example of why builders want to build wherever they can.

The chair reported that Richard Harris is again being retained by the town as interim consultant/land use manager, after a prior gap caused by limits on his allowed hours, not any problem with the working relationship.
The chair noted the Capital Planning Committee begins hearing department requests this week and expects to function more as a ranking committee again this year given competing priorities.

decisions.decision: Chair changed practice so open, non-agenda public comment is discouraged; residents should email the planning office to get items on the agenda instead.
Board agreed not to schedule a meeting three days before Christmas.
Chair to poll the board by email about shifting the December 8th meeting to December 15th to avoid a long gap into January.
Chair will draft written material for the next meeting laying out why the zoning bylaw needs a full rewrite, to support future funding requests for a consultant.
Board directed the storm water applicant and the abutter to try to work out details of the pipe/culvert plan before the November 10 meeting.

minutes.headline: Board votes to recommend MBTA Communities compliance via a density bump at Tritown, not new sites
not_audible: Names of the two abutters commenting on the Sunny Hill Road storm water permit are inconsistent in the captions (heard as 'Kenneth Patton', 'Christopher Halbut', 'Christopher Hall', and 'Ken') and could not be reconciled.
The exact status/outcome of the applicant's prior threatened lawsuit against the abutters was disputed on the record and not resolved in the captions.
Precise dollar figures for the 40R annual smart-growth payment to the town were given only as rough ranges.
Some board-edit discussion of specific bylaw section numbers and wording was hard to follow precisely from captions (e.g., exact subsection letters).

public_comment.topic: Objected to the Sunny Hill Road lot as too wet/dense to build on and defended board member Adam's right to ask new questions despite the prior board's earlier decision.
Described history of drainage pipes running onto his property, objected to lack of coordination on the new plan, and raised concern about a prior lawsuit threat from the developer.
Echoed the prior speaker's concerns, said abutters were not consulted on the revised plan, and asked the board to defer approval until there is written agreement the lawsuit threats will be dropped.
Raised concern that the property line between his lot and the applicant's had shifted about 8.8 feet and questioned whether that required conservation commission to revisit the plan.
Objected to the MBTA Communities law as an unfair state mandate not suited to what Lunenburg residents (seniors, young adults) actually need.

Asked detailed questions about which parcel is rezoned, whether it affects the town's 40R smart-growth payments and subsidized housing credits, and whether the state has reviewed the town's proposed bylaw language; praised the board's public engagement on the issue.
Praised the board's transparency on the MBTA Communities issue and asked the board to explain, for viewers, the unit-count and by-right requirements the state law imposes.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Planning Board endorsed a routine ANR lot-line adjustment for a Unitil substation expansion, then continued a contested storm water permit for 255 Sunny Hill Road to November 10 after abutters raised unresolved drainage-pipe and lawsuit concerns and outstanding taxes on the property surfaced. The board then closed public hearings and voted to recommend to town meeting both an MBTA Communities compliance bylaw (achieving compliance by raising the density cap at the existing Tritown development rather than opening new land) and a minor amendment removing a paving requirement from the common driveways bylaw, alongside routine committee reports and administrative votes.

what_happened.line: The board closed hearings and voted to recommend an MBTA Communities compliance bylaw that meets the state mandate by raising the density cap at the existing Tritown development rather than rezoning new land.

A contested storm water permit for 255 Sunny Hill Road was continued to November 10 after abutters raised unresolved drainage-pipe and past lawsuit concerns and outstanding taxes on the property came up.
The board also voted to recommend removing the paving requirement from the common driveways bylaw.
The chair changed practice so open, non-agenda public comment is discouraged going forward; residents are asked to email the planning office to get items placed on the agenda.

why_it_matters: The MBTA Communities recommendation goes to town meeting as a zoning bylaw vote, and choosing a density increase at Tritown over new sites is the mechanism the town is proposing to meet the state mandate.

The Sunny Hill Road continuance means the drainage dispute, the lawsuit concern between the applicant and an abutter, and the property's tax status remain open before any storm water permit is issued.
The change to public comment practice affects how residents get an item onto a Planning Board agenda going forward.
